fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can identify it without delay.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain a clear travel path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation along any walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Keep a clear, unobstructed path along at least one side of the main residence connecting the front driveway to the rear of the property.
• Mark any gate or opening that provides rear access so responders can locate it quickly without searching the perimeter.
• Keep any rear gate unlocked or secured with a combination lock, and share the combination with your local fire or police department.
• Post the water feature location visibly near the rear access point so responders are aware of it before moving through the area at night or in smoke.
• Thin dense vegetation between the detached structure and the main residence so responders can stage equipment and move freely between the two buildings.
• Identify and mark the best available staging area on the open lawn for emergency vehicles, keeping it free of stored items, equipment, or parked vehicles.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim lower branches on large trees near structures to reduce the chance of fire climbing from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Thin trees within the visible cluster closest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs and low vegetation growing directly against or touching any part of the structure.
• Separate mixed shrubs and ground vegetation from the base of large trees near the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation on both sides.
• Maintain the open green space between scattered trees and the structure by mowing or cutting back vegetation that is growing taller and denser over time.
• Keep vegetation trimmed back from the edges of the driveway to maintain full width for vehicle passage.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from around the base of trees and shrubs near the structure.
• Keep the area immediately around the water feature clear of accumulated dead leaves and debris that could carry fire.
